messages:
Ana: I opened a docs PR for an HSM key-rotation playbook tailored to sealed/offline Private installs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5379. Focus: rotation steps, PKCS#11 mapping, vendor quirks, and a safe rollback path for air-gapped sites.

Marco: Nice. Can we make the playbook non-prescriptive on exact key export formats? Some customers have different wrapped-key blobs. Recommend step templates instead of exact commands.

Ana: Yep — the doc now has templated steps and example commands for YubiHSM2 and Thales Luna. It also includes a minimal SDK snippet showing how to import a wrapped key into the Redwood agent after rotation. Example snippet:```python
# load wrapped key blob and import via SDK
from redwood_sdk import KmsClient
cli = KmsClient()
with open('rotated_blob.bin','rb') as f:
    blob = f.read()
cli.import_wrapped_key(blob, alias='rotated-main', allow_overwrite=False)
```

Vikram: Security checklist item: require an offline signing key held by ops to sign rotation manifests. Add a note about HSM-backed signing vs offline GPG.

Ana: Added a section on signing manifests and an example of using a detached GPG signature for the rotation plan. Also added a recommended quorum for approvals (2 infra + 1 security) for prod rotations.

Marco: For sealed networks, document how customers can stage rotation artifacts via an artifact bundle (tar + checksum + sig) and mirror import steps for both Linux mirror host and Windows offline host.

Ana: Done. The bundle flow shows: create tar -> generate sha256sum -> sign file -> copy to mirror -> instruct offline nodes to download and verify. PowerShell checksum example included:```powershell
if ((Get-FileHash .\\rotation-bundle.tar.gz -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne 'REPLACE_SHA256') { throw 'checksum mismatch' }
```

ops-bot: ci/rotation-docs-check started. Found 1 broken anchor in docs/hsm/rotation.md#windows-steps -> suggest rename to windows-rotation.

Ana: Fixed anchor and updated some cross-links. Quick Q: do we want a recommended maintenance window and canary strategy in the doc? I proposed: staggered host-by-host rotation with 5% canary for 24h, then 25% for 2h, then full roll.

Vikram: Good. Add rollback steps: immediate rebind to old key and a short validation checklist (ability to decrypt token, agent health, sample inference request). Include a note to keep old key around for at least 48h.

Ana: Added rollback flow and the validation commands for both Linux (curl to /health/local and check agent logs) and Windows (Get-Service + tail EventLog). Also a short systemd snippet for setting PKCS#11 lib env:```ini
[Service]
Environment=REDWOOD_PKCS11_LIB=/usr/local/lib/libyubihsm_pkcs11.so
```

Marco: Also call out vendor-specific driver install order and recommended reboots for Windows HSM middleware. Some vendors require middleware -> restart -> agent start.

Ana: Noted. I added vendor notes for YubiHSM2, Thales Luna, and SafeNet, with example PKCS#11 paths for Linux and Windows and a reminder about 32-bit vs 64-bit locations.

link-bot: link-checker/5379 completed. No broken links remaining, suggested tiny phrasing nits on firewall wording.

Ana: Swapped "open ports" text to "allow egress to mirror host on required ports (e.g., 443/445/2049)". Can folks do a quick review? I want this merged before next week's on-prem customer rotation window.

Vikram: Quick pass: LGTM. One small ask — add a short appendix with real-world failure examples (PKCS#11 path mismatch, unsigned driver block, checksum mismatch) and suggested debug commands.

Ana: Added Appendix C with failure scenarios and one-liner troubleshooting commands. Thanks! I'll merge when CI is green.
